items.stem: A company keeps 400 widgets on one shelf in the us-east-1 Region of Amazon Widget Store. The company expects to add 300 more widgets next month. A compliance rule states that all widgets must stay in us-east-1. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a second shelf in us-east-1 and put the new widgets on the second shelf.
options.why: A second shelf in the same Region gives the extra capacity and keeps every widget in us-east-1.

options.text: Keep all the widgets on the existing shelf in us-east-1 and add the new widgets to it.
options.why: The total is more than one shelf holds: a shelf holds [up to 500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets).

options.text: Pack the new widgets in crates and keep all the crates in us-east-1.
options.why: A crate holds [50 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-crate-capacity), so the company manages many crates, which is more operational overhead than one shelf.
options.misconception: treats a crate as long-term storage

options.text: Create a second shelf in us-west-2 and put the new widgets on the second shelf.
options.why: A shelf stores widgets in [one AWS Region](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-scope), so the new widgets leave us-east-1 and break the compliance rule.

items.explanation: The company will have more widgets than one shelf holds, because a shelf holds [up to 500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets). The widgets need two shelves. Both shelves are in us-east-1, so the compliance rule holds. One more shelf is one more resource to manage, which is the smallest change that works.
items.takeaway: When the widgets exceed the capacity of one shelf, add a shelf in the same Region.
items.twin: If the stem said "add 50 more widgets" instead: keep all the widgets on the existing shelf, because the total stays within [500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets).
items.say: One shelf has a capacity limit, so I'd add a second shelf in the same Region.

steps: I read the last sentence first: it asks for the solution with the LEAST operational overhead.
I mark the constraints: 400 widgets now, 300 more next month, and all widgets must stay in us-east-1.
Before I look at the options, I predict that the existing shelf has room, so the answer keeps one shelf.
I remove the shelf in us-west-2 because the widgets must stay in us-east-1. I remove the crates because many crates are more resources to manage.

Between the existing shelf and a second shelf the difference is capacity. My first idea breaks because the total is more than one shelf holds; the stem says LEAST operational overhead, so I add one shelf and nothing more.
Check: the second shelf in us-east-1 meets every constraint. Time: 90 seconds.

items.stem: A company keeps 400 widgets on one shelf in the us-east-1 Region of Amazon Widget Store. The company expects to add 50 more widgets next month. A compliance rule states that all widgets must stay in us-east-1. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create a second shelf in us-east-1 and put the new widgets on the second shelf.
options.why: It works, but a second shelf is one more resource to manage, and the existing shelf has room for the new widgets.
options.misconception: adds a resource that the requirements do not need

options.text: Keep all the widgets on the existing shelf in us-east-1 and add the new widgets to it.
options.why: The total stays within the [500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets) that one shelf holds, and nothing new needs management.

options.text: Pack the new widgets in a crate and keep the crate in us-east-1.
options.why: A crate is a container for shipping between Regions, so a crate adds a resource and solves a transport problem that the stem does not have.
options.misconception: treats a crate as long-term storage

options.text: Create a second shelf in us-west-2 and put the new widgets on the second shelf.
options.why: A shelf stores widgets in [one AWS Region](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-scope), so the new widgets leave us-east-1 and break the compliance rule.

items.explanation: After the change the company has fewer widgets than the limit of one shelf: a shelf holds [up to 500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets). The existing shelf is already in us-east-1, so the compliance rule holds. No new resource means no new operational work.
items.takeaway: Check the capacity first: when the widgets still fit, do not add a resource.
items.twin: If the stem said "add 300 more widgets" instead: create a second shelf in us-east-1, because one shelf holds [up to 500 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-max-widgets).

items.stem: A solutions architect creates a new shelf in Amazon Widget Store in the eu-west-1 Region and does not change any setting. The security team asks what to expect from the new shelf. Which statements about the new shelf are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The shelf is private, and its owner can read the shelf.
options.why: The architect changed no setting, and by default, a new shelf is [private](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-default-private).

options.text: The shelf stores its widgets in the eu-west-1 Region.
options.why: A shelf stores widgets in [one AWS Region](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-scope), the Region where the architect created the shelf.

options.text: Every user in the account can read the shelf.
options.why: At first [only its owner can read it](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-default-private), so other users in the account have no access.
options.misconception: assumes that account-wide read access is the default

options.text: The shelf and its widgets are visible in every Region.
options.why: A shelf is a [Regional resource](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-scope), so other Regions do not hold the shelf.

options.text: The architect can move the shelf to another Region later.
options.why: You [cannot move a shelf](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-move) to another Region.

items.explanation: The architect changed no setting, so the defaults apply. By default, a new shelf is [private](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-default-private). The shelf also stays in the Region where the architect created it, because a shelf stores widgets in [one AWS Region](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-scope).
items.takeaway: A new shelf is private and Regional until someone changes or copies it.
items.twin: If the stem said "the team needs the widgets in a second Region" instead: copy the shelf, because you [cannot move a shelf](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-move).

items.stem: A company stores widgets on a shelf in the us-east-1 Region of Amazon Widget Store. A partner in the ap-south-1 Region needs 40 of the widgets next week. The other widgets stay in us-east-1. Which Amazon Widget Store resource should the company use to send the 40 widgets?

options.text: A crate that the company ships to ap-south-1.
options.why: A crate is the container for widgets that travel between Regions, and the 40 widgets fit in one crate.

options.text: The existing shelf, moved from us-east-1 to ap-south-1.
options.why: You [cannot move a shelf](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-move) to another Region, and the other widgets stay in us-east-1.

options.text: A second shelf that the company creates in us-east-1.
options.why: A second shelf in us-east-1 adds capacity in the same Region and sends nothing to the partner.

options.text: A higher quota for shelves in us-east-1.
options.why: A quota changes how many shelves the account creates in a Region, and it sends nothing to another Region.
options.misconception: treats a quota as a way to reach another Region

items.explanation: The widgets travel to another Region, and a crate is the container that you ship between Regions. The 40 widgets fit in one crate, because a crate holds [50 widgets](../facts/widget.md#widget-crate-capacity). The shelf and the other widgets stay in us-east-1.
items.takeaway: Widgets that travel go in a crate; widgets that stay go on a shelf.
items.twin: If the stem said "the partner needs a full copy of the shelf" instead: [copy the shelf](../facts/widget.md#widget-shelf-move) to ap-south-1, because a copy keeps the first shelf in place.
